verdict.rationale: Babylon.js documents sprites and layers as part of its scene graph, so some of its own 2D building blocks exist. Nothing shows tilemaps, 2D physics, or a dedicated 2D workflow, and the listed physics engines are general integrations with no 2D mode described. Community comments describe the framework as having '3d concepts ingrained', which points to a 3D-first engine rather than first-class 2D. Missing for 10: tilemap support, 2D physics, a dedicated 2D workflow or camera, sprite-system depth docs, independent corroboration of 2D game development.

support.subject: As a game developer, 2D is a first-class workflow — sprites, tilemaps, 2D physics — not a 3D afterthought

citations.quote: Provides a complete scene graph with lights, cameras, materials, meshes, sprites, layers, animations, audio clips, GUI elements, and actions
